items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Mosley Interview, 1961-09-23
items.q: I used to go around listening to that... Old man Sims. George Sims. Oh yeah? Yeah, he was the manager of the band.

ctx.x: You remember when you were a boy, the real old band Professor Moneta tells about his brother, Norm, was it his brother? Yeah. Or his uncle. His uncle had a brass band way back. That would be when you were. No, I don't know. See, he's

way older than what I am, you know. Yeah, he's. I don't remember. It was Pacific brass band. Oh, the Pacific, yeah, I remember that. Remember Pacific? Oh yeah, I remember that. That's way back, isn't it? That's way back. I was nothing but a young kid then. Uh-huh. I used to go around listening to that. On that street called the Almas Street. It was in the four, five, in the six on the block. About there. The Almas? The Almas, yeah. They used to rehearse for that. The fella used to have been in a band. He used to,…

10, 11 years. I wonder why they called it Pacific. This is Pacific Street, isn't it? Yeah, yeah. Well, that's the old Pacific band. During that time they had the Pacific, there wasn't no such thing as a Tuxedo band. It wasn't existing. Is there any Pacific railroad or anything here that they might? Well, they had the Southern Pacific right back here, you know. Pacific right back here.
